titulo: Daily routine and reflexive verbs: Your daily routine

aula.objetivo: Talk about your daily routine with reflexive verbs (mi alzo, mi lavo, mi vesto), adverbs of frequency and sequence words, and use «ci vediamo» and other reciprocal verbs. Avoid the English-speaker traps: dropping the reflexive pronoun, writing «my» before body parts, and avoiding the double negative.

blocos.titulo: Order and frequency: «prima, poi, dopo», «mai», «di solito»
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to put actions in order, use «prima» (first), «poi» (then), «dopo» (after, later) and «infine» (finally): «Prima mi lavo, poi mi vesto». STEP 2: English puts adverbs of frequency before the verb («I always get up», «I never get up early»). Italian usually puts them after it: «Mi alzo sempre alle sette». At the start of the sentence, «di solito» (usually) works well: «Di solito faccio colazione al bar». STEP 3: with «mai» (never), the negation has two parts. After the verb, «mai» needs «non» before the verb: «Non mi sveglio mai presto». English does not allow the double negative, but Italian requires it. STEP 4: to give the frequency per period, use «tutti i giorni», «ogni mattina», «due volte alla settimana». STEP 5: for parts of the day, Italian uses an article: «la mattina», «il pomeriggio», «la sera», «la notte»: «La mattina bevo un caffè». «La sera» is the evening and «la notte» is the late night. STEP 6: «andare a letto» is «to go to bed», and it uses «a» (not «in»). STEP 7: use «prima di» + infinitive for «before doing»: «Prima di uscire mi lavo i denti» (Before going out I brush my teeth). English uses the «-ing» form there; Italian uses the infinitive.
blocos.comparacao: English adverb order is strict (before the verb), Italian is more flexible, with the adverb usually after the verb. The double negative is the big new idea: «non… mai» is not an error, it is the standard way to say «never». And English «before going» is a gerund, while Italian says «prima di uscire», with the infinitive.
